ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: judging a weapon
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: One number from 1 to 10 for every weapon, what it is good and weak at, how it suits each colonist, and the best weapon for each
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A sniper rifle isn't marked down for being poor at five cells, nor a shotgun at forty: each weapon is judged at the distances its role is for.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Every weapon a colonist can wield, from the game, its DLCs and your mods, has a rating from 1.0 to 10.0 at the top of its info card, worked out from what it really does in a fight by the game's own rules. Beside it: sub-ratings, colour-coded tags with the reason for each, a line in plain words, and its effects, counted or only named. Rimfolk's weapon card draws its damage by distance and sets it against what a colonist holds.

points.li: A colonist of Shooting 8 and Melee 8 with no traits fights the enemies a colony meets after its first year: a quarter raiders in plain clothes, two fifths in flak, a fifth in marine armour, the rest mechanoids. In the open, in daylight, without cover.

Guns: the chance to hit at each distance (the shooter's accuracy to the power of the distance, times the weapon's accuracy there), armour against its piercing, aim, burst and cooldown, blasts and their scatter, fire, stuns and EMP. A gun that can't reach a raider's rifle at 31 cells loses up to a quarter; damage dealt from beyond it counts double.
Melee weapons: the blows the game picks (its best three times in four), the fighter's hit chance and the target's dodge, armour, and what each blow carries.

What it does to whoever holds it counts too (move speed, aim, melee hit, dodge, damage taken), and so do the abilities it grants, up to half again its own worth. What a mod's own code does is valued where its code was read, and otherwise named and marked rough.

5.5 is the middle: about an assault rifle, a steel longsword or a warhammer. Near the middle a point is about a third more damage for a gun and a fifth more for a melee weapon; the scale flattens toward both ends.
A weapon's own quality and stuff change its rating, by the game's own stats: a legendary blade hits harder, an awful rifle aims worse.
An Odyssey unique weapon is rated with its rolled traits (burst, stopping power, its damage, extra damage, and what the traits do to its numbers); a persona weapon with its traits and its bond.
Biocoding doesn't change the rating; the card says who it is coded to.

li.heading: Tags
li.text: Each weapon shows its most telling tags, seven at most, each given by a rule on its own numbers with the reason on its tooltip. Six kinds, each with its colour and its own mark: strengths (green, up), weaknesses (red, down), risks (orange, a warning), specials (violet, a star), roles (blue, a diamond) and what it needs (grey, a dot). The same tags and colours are on the tier list of every weapon in your mods.

points.li: The weapon's own picture, large, framed in the colour of its quality (awful brown, poor grey, normal light, good green, excellent blue, masterwork violet, legendary gold) and naming it: the weapon as it looks in hand, its stuff, its style, a unique or persona weapon's own look. Small pictures wherever the card lists other weapons.

The badge, the tags as chips, the line in plain words and the sub-ratings; a chart of damage per second by distance against no armour, flak, marine armour and mechanoids (bars by armour for a melee weapon); the situations it is best for and weak in; every effect; the key numbers.

For a colonist: their own rating from their real shooting accuracy or melee hit chance, aim, cooldowns and blows, each step that moves it named (their skill, a careful shooter, a brawler, their sight and gear). What stops them using it: incapable of violence, biocoded to someone else, a heavy weapon they can't carry.
It opens from a button at the foot of the game's info card, a button on a weapon selected on the map, and a small button beside each weapon on the gear tab.

With "Open Rimfolk's weapon card first" (on at first), opening the info for a weapon anywhere (the "i" button on the gear tab, Nice Inventory Tab, a trade screen, a list, the research or architect tab, the inspect pane) opens this card instead of the game's. Its button "All the game's stats" opens the game's own card for the same weapon, and the game's card keeps its button back. Links followed inside the game's card stay in it.
A weapon's kind (from the research or architect tab, or a list) is rated as made: normal quality, in its usual stuff (steel where it takes metal), and its card says so.
Who should carry this: the colonists it suits best, by the same scores as the suggestions below, each with what it adds over what they have of its kind. A click shows it for them.

li.heading: The best weapon for each colonist
li.text: From what the colony has: what lies in storage they can reach and isn't forbidden (in a stockpile, on a shelf, on an outfit stand), what they carry themselves, and what another colonist holds when a trade is better for both or for the colony. Shown on the gear tab, on the weapon card, and for the whole colony on the Defenses page ("Weapon suggestions", on). On the gear tab each suggestion is a row of its own: in Nice Inventory Tab's equipment box under the weapons held, or under the game's list, in a dashed frame marked "Suggested" so it never looks like a weapon held, with the weapon's picture, its name and quality, its rating for them and the gain, why in a line, and its buttons. With nothing better to suggest, one quiet line says so, and its tooltip says what was compared ("Say when there's no better weapon", on).

points.li: Each colonist's own rating of each weapon comes first: their skill, traits and body. Then their passion for Shooting or Melee, the fights the colony meets (mechanoids, armoured raiders, crowds, sieges, read from the raids it met lately, and a gate it holds when it has drawn a defense line) and their work: a hunter wants a gun or bow that doesn't explode, a doctor or crafter a light weapon. A weapon their faith holds noble counts in its favour.

Never suggested: a weapon their faith despises, one coded or bonded to someone else, a heavy weapon they can't carry, anything for someone incapable of violence, a gun for a brawler or someone who can't shoot. Leaving their own bonded persona weapon unused takes a much bigger gain, and the line says what it costs.
Only a gain worth the walk is suggested: 0.6 of a point, about a fifth more damage for a gun. An assault rifle to a charge rifle is suggested, a longsword to a uranium one isn't.

One choice for the whole colony, so two colonists are never told to take the same weapon: the biggest gains first, each weighed by how much the colonist fights, then swaps between them while the colony's total rises. Then trades between two colonists, then a sidearm with Simple Sidearms (within its weights) and a weapon for the off hand with Dual Wield where both hands together add enough.

How much a colonist fights: their best of Shooting and Melee against the colony's best, their time drafted and their kills and shots fired (the game's own records) against the colony's most, a hunter a little more, a doctor or crafter a little less. A doctor who is rarely drafted counts for less in a fight than the colony's best shot.

A trade is suggested when it is better for both, or when the colony gains clearly even though one of the two gives up some: the one who gains gains at least a point, and the gain and the loss, each weighed by how much its colonist fights, add up to 0.8 or more. A weak shot holding the best gun hands it to the good shot and takes theirs: "Charge rifle to Ana (+1.9), Bautista takes her revolver (-0.6): the colony gains, and Bautista rarely fights." A trade that only moves value between two who fight alike isn't suggested, and nobody is left without a weapon.

A lucky weapon (a colonist's lucky charm) or an heirloom they carry is never a bar: giving it up counts a little when one weapon or trade is weighed against another (another weapon of its kind may win over a slightly better one), never enough to stop a suggestion, and the line always says it with the real moods, as "Bautista would be upset to give up his lucky autopistol (mood -4 without it, +3 with it)". Another weapon of the same kind keeps the luck, and with Simple Sidearms the old weapon kept as a sidearm keeps it too.
Each comes with why in a line, as "Charge rifle: +1.4 for Ana: her Shooting 14 makes its accuracy count, and it pierces the armour your last raids wore."

The buttons give real orders, walked out on the map: the game's Equip, Simple Sidearms' own job for a sidearm, Dual Wield's own for the off hand, and a trade where one walks over to the other. "Equip all suggested" on the Defenses page only gives the orders. "Not now" sets a colonist's suggestions aside for ten days.

li.heading: Colonists who ask
li.text: When a clearly better weapon lies unused in storage (twice the gain a suggestion needs), a colonist now and then says so in one line of their own, naming it, where it lies and why: "That charge rifle in the stockpile would do far more against the mechanoids we keep meeting." Only in their free time at home, never in danger, drafted, downed or not themselves; at most once in five days each and once a day in the colony, never while their suggestions are set aside. A quiet entry stays in This week while it still lies there; a click opens their gear ("Colonists ask for better weapons", on). Colonists propose trades the same way, to the other once the two are together and both still hold what they speak of: the one who would gain asks ("Bautista, that charge rifle would do more in my hands, will you take my revolver?"), the one who rarely fights or can barely use their weapon offers it ("You should have this charge rifle, Ana, I can barely aim it."). Nobody offers up their own lucky weapon or heirloom, though the other may still ask for it. Its entry in This week gives the order to trade.

points.li: Simple Sidearms: each weapon a colonist carries is rated for them, and the card names their sensible pair, the best gun and the best melee weapon they hold or carry, a sidearm only within its default weights (2.7 kg for a gun, 1.9 kg for a blade).

Dual Wield: the off-hand weapon is rated with Dual Wield's penalties, its cooldown 20% longer and its aim 10% worse, more the lower the skill (at skill 8, 80% and 16%), and both hands together when both are guns or both blades.
RunAndGun: whether the weapon can be fired on the move, 10% less accurate, and what it rates then.
Melee Animation: whether it animates the weapon's blows, how many execution moves are open to it at the colonist's Melee, and whether it is long enough for friendly duels.

Nice Inventory Tab and the game's gear tab: a small badge with the rating beside each weapon, its tooltip the tags and the colonist's own rating. On Nice Inventory Tab a click on the badge opens Rimfolk's card to compare, and the suggestions sit in its equipment box as rows of their own.
